text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementTechnologyCreating Fake People is a Terrible IdeaSo why is a company pursuing digital avatars with such gusto?ASBy Anil Seth7:00 AM CDT on October 7, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleA few days ago the “human computing company” Tavos announced a product called Griffin. Griffin is a “human interaction model.” Supposedly, it is the first AI product to pass a video version of the Turing Test, meaning that real people cannot tell the difference between talking to Griffin and talking to a real person—even when audio and video are allowed.Powered By 10 ShareNextStayThis is a terrible development. The consequences for society are likely to be disastrous—perhaps even worse than the havoc wrought by social media. People will be scammed out of their savings, mental illness will explode, loneliness will be exploited. Collectively we’ll become less able to tell reality from fantasy, tearing at the fabric of a society already under considerable stress. Many more horrors will likely follow that we can’t even conceive of yet. (Here’s one suggestion: How about people deliberately abusing their digital avatars to satisfy the darkest corners of their psychology?)Read More: “AI Already Knows Us Too Well”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
